# unifi_network_device (Resource)

A UniFi network device (access point, switch, or gateway) identified by MAC. The single resource adopts the device if it's pending, then manages its config (name, LED, management network, and per-port `port_overrides`) and exposes read-only telemetry. By default `terraform destroy` reverts the Terraform-managed port overrides and drops the device from state; set `forget_on_destroy = true` to instead forget (unadopt) the device. **Adoption and config-write are HIL-unverified — see the provider TODO.**



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mac` (String) Device MAC address (the natural key). The device must be visible to the controller (adopted, or pending adoption). Immutable — changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `forget_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true`, `terraform destroy` forgets (unadopts) the device instead of just reverting the managed port overrides. Defaults to `false`. Guard production devices with `prevent_destroy`.
- `led_override` (String) Status-LED behavior: `on`, `off`, or `default` (follow the site setting).
- `led_override_color` (String) LED color as a hex string (when the model supports a colored LED).
- `led_override_color_brightness` (Number) LED brightness (0–100), when the model supports it.
- `mgmt_network_id` (String) The device's **management VLAN** (`unifi_network_network` id). The device 802.1Q-tags its own control-plane traffic (inform, adoption) with this network's VLAN, so it reaches the controller and gets its IP on that subnet **regardless of the upstream switch port's untagged/native VLAN** — an AP on a port whose `native_network_id` is `iot` still lands on the management subnet. Distinct from `config_network` (the device's IP-addressing mode: dhcp/static), which this provider does not model.
- `name` (String) Device display name.
- `port_overrides` (Attributes Map) Per-port configuration, keyed by physical port number (e.g. `"1"`). Terraform manages only the ports listed here: each is merged onto the controller's existing override (unmodeled keys are preserved), undeclared ports are left untouched, and removing a port reverts it to defaults. **On import, every port with a live override is captured** so `terraform plan -generate-config-out` reflects the switch — keep the ports you want to manage in config (dropping one reverts it, as does `terraform destroy`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--port_overrides))

### Read-Only

- `adopted` (Boolean) Whether the device is adopted by this controller.
- `id` (String) Controller object ID (`_id`).
- `ip` (String) Current management IP.
- `model` (String) Hardware model code.
- `state` (Number) Controller state code (`1` = connected).
- `type` (String) Device type (`uap`, `usw`, `ugw`, `udm`, …).
- `version` (String) Running firmware version.

<a id="nestedatt--port_overrides"></a>
### Nested Schema for `port_overrides`

Optional:

- `autoneg` (Boolean) Auto-negotiate link speed/duplex.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Administratively disable (shut down) the port — no link, no forwarding. The controller has no direct disable field; it derives `forward=disabled` from `tagged_vlan_mgmt=block_all` with no native VLAN, so set this instead of hand-building that pair. Setting `false` re-enables a disabled port to the default trunk; to put it on a specific VLAN instead, omit `disabled` and set the VLAN fields. Mutually exclusive with `port_profile_id`, `native_network_id`, `voice_network_id`, `excluded_network_ids`, and a non-`block_all` `tagged_vlan_mgmt`. A bound port profile governs the port, so disable the profile instead.
- `dot1x_ctrl` (String) 802.1X control mode.
- `dot1x_idle_timeout` (Number) 802.1X idle timeout (seconds).
- `egress_rate_limit_enabled` (Boolean) Enable an egress rate limit.
- `egress_rate_limit_kbps` (Number) Egress rate limit in kbps (when enabled).
- `excluded_network_ids` (Set of String) Tagged networks to exclude when `tagged_vlan_mgmt = custom`.
- `full_duplex` (Boolean) Forced full duplex (when `autoneg = false`).
- `isolation` (Boolean) Isolate this port from other isolated ports.
- `lldpmed_enabled` (Boolean) Enable LLDP-MED.
- `multicast_router_mode` (String) Multicast router mode.
- `name` (String) Port label.
- `native_network_id` (String) Untagged/native network (`unifi_network_network` id) — the port's VLAN intent.
- `poe_mode` (String) Power over Ethernet: `auto`, `pasv24`, `passthrough`, or `off` (varies by switch). HIL-unverified.
- `port_keepalive_enabled` (Boolean) Enable port keep-alive.
- `port_profile_id` (String) Bind the port to a `unifi_network_port_profile` (its `id`). The profile then governs the port's VLAN behavior, so leave the inline VLAN intent (`native_network_id`, `tagged_vlan_mgmt`) unset — the controller nulls them (and the derived `forward`) once a profile is bound.
- `port_security_enabled` (Boolean) Restrict the port to specific MAC addresses.
- `port_security_mac_addresses` (Set of String) Allowed MAC addresses when `port_security_enabled = true`.
- `speed` (Number) Forced link speed in Mbps (when `autoneg = false`).
- `stp_bpdu_guard` (Boolean) Enable BPDU guard.
- `stp_edge_state` (String) STP edge-port state.
- `stp_port_mode` (Boolean) Participate in spanning tree.
- `tagged_vlan_mgmt` (String) Tagged-VLAN handling: `auto` (allow all), `block_all` (native only), or `custom` (allow all but `excluded_network_ids`). The controller derives `forward` from this.
- `voice_network_id` (String) Voice VLAN network (`unifi_network_network` id).

Read-Only:

- `forward` (String) VLAN forwarding mode, **derived by the controller** (read-only) from `native_network_id` + `tagged_vlan_mgmt` + `excluded_network_ids`: `all` (trunk), `native`, `customize`, or `disabled` (set `disabled = true` rather than aiming for this). Set the intent fields instead — the controller computes this. (Binding a port profile governs it.)
